balance.priceIncreaseDe: Until then you have a special right to cancel effective on the day of the increase (§ 41 (5) EnWG).

Special payments = refunds (+), back-payments and extra advance payments (−) outside the advance schedule; both feed into the balance. Tap to see the individual items; they are maintained in the contract management.

estimatedTitle.other: {days} days estimated (after the last known stock)

tank.noCapacity: No tank capacity set — enter it on the meter to see the stock curve.
tank.noteMeasured: Consumption calculated from known stock levels up to {date}, estimated afterwards.
tank.noteEstimated: Stock and consumption are estimated from the initial stock and the deliveries. A delivery “filled to full” or a tank reading makes them exact.

tank.warnExhausted: By calculation the tank has been empty since {date}. Is a delivery or a tank reading missing?
tank.warnNoCalibration: No consumption rate yet: it needs two known tank levels at least 14 days apart (initial stock, delivery “Filled to full”, tank reading) or two deliveries.

tank.levelsEmpty: No tank reading yet. A reading makes the calculation exact up to that day.

tank.levelRange: Please enter a level between 0 and {cap} {unit}.

toast.readingConfirmed: Reading confirmed – it now counts in the analysis.

billCheck.hint: Recalculates the gas bill: per section m³ × volume correction factor × calorific value = kWh, like the lines of a supplier bill. A new section starts at every reading and every calorific-value change.
billCheck.empty: No sections in the chosen range.
billCheck.formula: kWh = m³ × volume correction factor × calorific value. The supplier estimates intermediate readings at calorific-value boundaries; here the reading interval is split day-exactly.
billCheck.errRange: Please choose a valid range (from before to).

kind.interpolated: substitute value — no meter reading on this day, interpolated day-exact between the enclosing readings

billCheck.legend: Reading type: no suffix = meter reading · {est} = reading recorded as estimated · {int} = interpolated value: there is no meter reading on this day, it is interpolated day-exact between the enclosing readings — exactly where the supplier estimates too (calorific-value and period boundaries). The more rows without {int}, the less is estimation.

gapsN.one: {count} section without an enclosing reading — consumption is missing there.
gapsN.other: {count} sections without an enclosing reading — consumption is missing there.

billCheck.hintGeneric: Recalculates the annual bill: per section consumption × unit price plus fixed costs, like the lines of a supplier bill. A new section starts at every reading and every price change.

fw.title: District heating: connection and key figures
fw.hint: Found on the bill or the heat supplier’s price sheet. Capacity and metering charges count as fixed costs; the network CO₂ factor replaces the general value for district heating.

hint.termOver24: Note: the minimum term is longer than 24 months. In Germany, an initial term this long is invalid for consumers (§ 309 no. 9 BGB).

groupPrices.title: Unit price per meter (e.g. peak/off-peak)
groupPrices.hint: One standing charge but a separate unit price per register — e.g. for peak and off-peak. Empty = unit price above.

priceImport.title: Apply monthly prices
priceImport.preview: The file contains prices for {n} months ({from} to {to}). Each applies from the first of the month; prices with the same effective date are replaced.

revenue.title: Credit notes from the direct marketer
revenue.hint: With direct marketing the revenue follows the market value. Enter the credit note — for its period it replaces kWh × price.

gridTou.title: § 14a module 3: time-variable grid fee
gridTou.hint: Standard tariff and time windows from your grid operator’s price sheet (grid fee per kWh). A window across midnight is two windows. Evaluated under Insights → Flexibility.
gridTou.netHint: Unticked, the amounts apply as entered (gross, as on the bill). Ticked, the app adds VAT to them — the rate it also uses for the wholesale price.

phaseGroup.shadowHint: Quotes (shadow contracts) are what-if calculations and do not count towards costs, balance or forecast.

gasFactor.why: The correction factor and the calorific value depend on the supply point (altitude, pressure) and on the gas in the network, not on the supplier: they stay the same when you switch, and every gas bill states them. That is why they are set once in the settings and apply to every contract.

advance.dueDates: Due dates according to the bill: {dates}, then yearly on the same days

info.title: Multiple meters per utility
info.text: — e.g. hot water & heating (gas) or peak/off-peak & wallbox (electricity). Each meter has its own device history (meter swaps are calculated without loss) and can carry its own contracts.
info.topologyText: Sub-meters are subtracted from the parent meter; groups combine several meters in the dashboard.

deleteGroup.title: Dissolve group?
deleteGroup.message: Dissolve group “{name}”? The assigned meters are kept and are only removed from the group.

deleteMeter.title: Delete meter?
deleteMeter.message: Delete meter “{name}” and its device history? Readings and contracts must be removed first.

modal.activeHint: Clear this when the meter is out of service: its history still counts in every total, but it no longer appears in the reading entry and raises no warnings.
modal.initialStockPriceHint: Leave empty to use the price of the first delivery.

roleHint.strom: Heat pump: this electricity meter measures the heating and counts towards the efficiency figure.
roleHint.wasser: Hot water: the app also shows the heat needed for it (calculated value under HeizkostenV § 9). Garden: water that does not go into the sewer.
roleHint.pv_erzeugung: Battery: charging and discharging as separate meters, apart from generation.
roleHint.waerme: Consumption: heat that arrives in the home (counts as heating energy). Heat pump output: does not count as heating energy, otherwise it would be counted twice next to the heating electricity.

modal.captureHint: Consumption per period: for values that already come as consumption – such as the monthly consumption information from the metering service. Switching is possible while the meter has no data.
modal.maloHint: For switching supplier; shown on the bill. MaLo: 11 digits; MeLo: 33 characters starting with “DE”.

replace.title: Meter swap: {name}
replace.intro: Closes the currently open device with a final reading and creates a new device. Consumption across the swap is calculated correctly automatically — no more “negative consumption” after a swap.

replace.confirmSummary: On {date} the old device is closed at {oldFinal} {unit} and the new one starts at {newInitial} {unit}. This cannot be undone in the app.
replace.fromInbox: Prefilled from the inbox – check the values against the letter once more.

import.title: Import readings: {name}
import.intro: Reads readings from a CSV file for the meter {name}. Before importing, a preview shows every row and what it will do — an existing reading on the same day is replaced.
import.formatHint: Separator ; or , · date DD/MM/YYYY, DD.MM.YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD (day before month) · decimal comma allowed · columns note and estimated optional · a header row is detected automatically.
import.dropZone: Drop a CSV file here or click to select
import.dropZoneAria: Select a CSV file or drop it here

mergeModal.intro: Combine several meters into a group — e.g. off-peak + peak electricity or several wallboxes. The group shows the total on the overview; the meters themselves stay separate and unchanged.
mergeModal.needTwo: Please select at least two meters
mergeModal.needName: Please provide a group name or choose an existing group

baseline.title: Baseline dates
baseline.hint: After building work the house consumes differently for good. Enter the date here — the analyses then start from that point, while older months stay visible but no longer feed the model. A future date may be recorded in advance; it only takes effect once reached.
baseline.label: Description
baseline.none: No baseline date recorded — every analysis uses the full history.
baseline.dateRequired: Please give a date for the baseline

periodImport.intro: Import consumption per period for “{name}” from a CSV file.
periodImport.formatHint: One line each: a month and the consumption ({unit}), or from; to; consumption; note. Header optional; overlapping periods are skipped.

pv.title: PV system
pv.plugIn: Plug-in solar device (balcony system, no feed-in meter)
pv.plugInHint: Up to 2,000 Wp of modules and 800 VA inverter; registration only in the German market master data register. The app estimates self-consumption with the share from the settings.
pv.hint: Investment and commissioning date give the payback. The storage capacity belongs on the meter with the role “Battery – charging” and gives the full cycles.

heatPumpLink.title: Heat pump electricity meter
heatPumpLink.hint: For the seasonal performance factor (heat ÷ electricity). Electricity meters with the heat pump role are offered.
heatPumpLink.none: No electricity meter with the heat pump role set up.

lang.title: Language & country / Sprache
lang.hint: The language applies to this device; without a choice of its own it follows the installation's default language, which also sets the annual report, CSV files and Home Assistant. The country sets number and date formats, currency and time zone; when you change it, the app suggests matching defaults.

physical.title: Physical constants
physical.hint: Conversion and heating-degree-day base — affect all analyses.

co2.title: CO₂ emission factors
co2.hint: Grams of CO₂ per consumption unit, for the emission estimate.
co2.list: Factors per utility and electricity per year

billing.title: Billing cycle
billing.hint: The settlement date is the first day of the billing period, per utility in the format DD-MM: 01-09 means 1 September to 31 August, 01-01 the calendar year. The balance of open contracts runs to the day before, the last day of the period; contracts with a maintained end date use that end. Recorded bills take precedence.

contractReminders.title: Reminders
contractReminders.hint: Three levels before a contract ends or its notice deadline; for reminders the advance warning and the grace period until “overdue”.

water.title: Water reference values
water.hint: Household size, per-capita reference and the bands of the saving index.

regression.title: Regression & forecast
regression.hint: Filters for the regression basis and parameters of the forecast model.

dashboard.title: Display
dashboard.hint: Time span of the overview and the forecast; when a missing reading is flagged.

building.title: Building & efficiency
building.hint: Reference values for the efficiency class (kWh/m²·a) and the heating-energy benchmark.

delivery.title: Energy sources (delivery)
delivery.hint: Energy content of delivery-based fuels and the tank warning threshold.

remindersRec.title: Recommendations & distribution
remindersRec.hint: Thresholds of the recommendations and the base-load share used to spread heating oil and pellets over the days.

location.title: Location (Open-Meteo)
location.hint: Coordinates for the weather sync of the temperature series.

embedding.title: Embedding
embedding.hint: Other sites may not embed Energietracker – this protects against hijacked clicks. For a webpage card on a Home Assistant dashboard, enter its address here.

attachments.title: Receipts
attachments.hint: Photos of meter readings and PDF files are kept in the data directory and go into the backup.

ocr.title: Text recognition in the home network
ocr.hint: Suggests the meter reading from a photo – using your own service, whose address and interface are set in the “Reading documents” card under “Local”. Only the image model and time limit are here. Nothing goes to a cloud service.

tenancy.title: Home and hot water
tenancy.hint: If you rent, the Costs area gets the “Tenancy” page. The energy source sets the CO₂ value of the heat.

co2price.title: CO₂ price
co2price.hint: The CO₂ price in fuel (BEHG). Without your own values the country profile applies; the scenario shows in the forecast what a higher price would cost.

pv.title: Photovoltaics
pv.hint: Assumptions for a plug-in solar device without a feed-in meter.

reference.title: Own reference values
reference.hint: For the benchmark on the overview. The app ships no tables; enter the values an electricity or heating benchmark gives you.

evcc.title: evcc in your home network
evcc.hint: Fetches the charging sessions from evcc when you tap “Fetch from evcc” in the wallbox view. Only addresses in your own network. Empty = off; the CSV file from evcc always works.

hosts.title: Host names
hosts.hint: List the names you use to open the app. It then only answers to these names – without sign-in this protects against other websites that point their name at your address (DNS rebinding). IP addresses always work.

updates.title: New versions
updates.hint: Once a day the app can check on GitHub whether a newer version exists. GitHub only sees your server’s address, no data from the app.

flex.title: Flexibility
flex.hint: What the Flexibility page uses for “Your lever” where nothing is measured. Empty = sample value; what you enter, the page and the annual report call “your value”.

environment.title: Environment
environment.hint: If you run several installations (test, home, holiday flat), you see next to the logo which one you are in.

hdd_base_temp.label: HDD base temperature
hdd_base_temp.hint: Heating limit — days below count as heating days.

co2_gas.label: CO₂ gas
co2_gas.hint: BAFA: 201 g/kWh, based on the net calorific value. The app counts gas by gross calorific value (z-number × calorific value), hence × 0.906 = 182.

co2_strom.label: CO₂ electricity
co2_strom.hint: Applies to years before the first yearly value — without yearly values, to all years.

co2_wasser.label: CO₂ water
co2_wasser.hint: For treatment and pumping per m³ of water — an estimate without an official source.

co2_fernwaerme.label: CO₂ district heating
co2_fernwaerme.hint: BAFA flat rate. Your heat network’s own value is more accurate — ask your supplier.

co2_heizoel.label: CO₂ heating oil
co2_heizoel.hint: BAFA, based on the net calorific value — as the app calculates heating oil.

co2_pellets.label: CO₂ pellets
co2_pellets.hint: BAFA, CO₂ equivalents including the upstream chain.

billing_cycle_anchor_gas.label: Settlement date gas: first day of the billing period

billing_cycle_anchor_strom.label: Settlement date electricity: first day of the billing period

billing_cycle_anchor_wasser.label: Settlement date water: first day of the billing period

wasser_personen_anzahl.label: Number of people
wasser_personen_anzahl.hint: For the water saving index: litres per person and day compared with the reference.

wasser_personen_referenz.label: Reference
wasser_personen_referenz.hint: BDEW 2024: 122 L per person and day (Germany).

wasser_sparindex_gut.label: Saving index — good up to
wasser_sparindex_gut.hint: Index ≤ this value is considered unremarkable.

wasser_sparindex_warnung.label: Saving index — warning from
wasser_sparindex_warnung.hint: Index ≥ this value indicates saving potential.

min_days_period.label: Min. days per period
min_days_period.hint: Months with fewer recorded days (partial months) stay out of the heating signature and anomalies.

min_hdd_regression.label: Min. HDD for regression
min_hdd_regression.hint: Months with fewer degree days stay out of the heating signature — in summer the base load drives consumption, not the weather.

blend_max.label: Max. blend weight
blend_max.hint: Highest weight of the weather model in the forecast; the rest comes from the seasonal profile. 0.8 means at least 20% seasonal profile.

forecast_months.label: Forecast horizon
forecast_months.hint: How many months the forecast looks ahead (1–24). Default of the forecast view.

forecast_model.label: Default model
forecast_model.hint: Model for forecast and tariff comparison. Linear suits most homes; the analysis shows which one explains your data best.

segmented_split_mode.label: Segment breakpoint
segmented_split_mode.hint: auto = fitted from data, fixed = fixed HDD value below.

anomaly_threshold.label: Anomaly threshold
anomaly_threshold.hint: From what deviation (in units of spread σ) a month counts as unusual in the analysis. Smaller means more sensitive.

dashboard_months.label: Months on dashboard
dashboard_months.hint: How many months the history on the overview shows (3–36).

alert_days_since_reading.label: Warn after
alert_days_since_reading.hint: If the last reading is older, the meter appears under “To do” and the consumption view reminds you.

wohnflaeche_m2.label: Living area
wohnflaeche_m2.hint: Heated area — denominator of the efficiency metric.

gebaeudetyp.label: Building type
gebaeudetyp.hint: Multi-family means three or more flats.

heizoel_kwh_per_l.label: Heating oil energy content

heatAdjusted.text: Consumption converted to a year with normal weather. It shows whether more or less heating was used, regardless of how cold the winter was.

hdd.text: A measure of how cold a period was: the colder, the more heating degree days.

balance.text: The difference between the cost of consumption and the advance payments made. Credit: more paid than used. Additional payment: consumption cost more.

advance.text: A fixed amount paid to the supplier every month. The annual bill compares it with the actual costs.

profileFactor.text: The own market price relative to the monthly average. Below 1, the electricity tended to run in cheap hours.

module14a.text: Time-variable grid fee for controllable devices such as heat pumps: in certain hours the grid fee is lower.

subMeter.text: A meter behind another one, for example for a wallbox or the garden. Its consumption is already in the main meter and does not count twice.

prepayment.text: A monthly amount paid to the landlord for heating, water and operating costs; the service charge statement settles it against the costs.

co2Split.text: In German rented homes, tenant and landlord share the CO₂ costs of heating in ten stages (CO2KostAufG).

baseline.text: A date that has been entered, for example a renovation. The report compares consumption per degree day before and after.

noticeDeadline.text: The last day on which notice must reach the supplier for the contract to end at the end of its term.

estimated.text: For days without a reading, Energietracker uses an estimate based on previous consumption.

efficiency.text: A rating of heating energy per square metre of living space on a scale from A+ (very good) to H, similar to an energy certificate.

workingPrice.text: The price per unit consumed, for example cents per kWh.

basePrice.text: A fixed amount per month, regardless of consumption.

selfConsumption.text: Solar power used in the house instead of being fed into the grid.

autarky.text: The share of electricity consumption covered by the own system.

feedIn.text: Solar power that goes into the grid; it earns a feed-in payment.

jaz.text: How much heat a heat pump makes from one kilowatt hour of electricity, over a whole year. 3 means: 1 kWh of electricity becomes 3 kWh of heat.

tankBook.text: Deliveries and stock levels of heating oil or pellets; from these, Energietracker calculates consumption and how long the stock lasts.

hdd.text: How cold it was, measured against the heating threshold: per day the difference between the threshold and the daily mean, 0 on warm days. More degree days mean more heating demand.

heatingLimit.text: The outdoor temperature below which heating starts — usually 15 °C in Germany (setting “HDD base temperature”). Warmer days count no degree days.

heatingSignature.text: The relation between degree days and consumption, calculated from your own months: how much your home uses per degree day and how large the weather-independent base load is.

baseload.text: The part of consumption that does not depend on the weather — hot water, cooking or standby, for example. It occurs in summer too.

weatherAdjusted.text: Consumption converted to normal weather at your location (climate normal). Only the weather share is converted, so a mild and a cold winter become comparable.

climateNormal.text: Average degree days per calendar month from 30 years of weather data for your location. The basis for forecast and weather adjustment.

r2.text: How well a model explains your monthly values — from 0 (not at all) to 1 (completely). From about 0.7 the relation is clear.

models.text: Linear: a straight line. Polynomial: a slightly curved line. Robust (Huber): like linear, but insensitive to outliers. Segmented: two lines with a break point where heating starts. Sigmoid: an S-curve that flattens in severe cold.

movingAverage.text: The mean of the last 3 or 6 months. It smooths out single outliers and shows the trend.

forecastBlend.text: The forecast blends the weather model with your seasonal profile (average per calendar month). The better the model fits (R²), the more it counts — up to the “Max. blend weight”.

anomaly.text: A month that differs clearly from what was expected for exactly this month. The threshold (σ) says by how many units of spread it must differ at least.

balance.text: The difference between the cost of your consumption and the advance payments made (including special payments). Credit: you paid more and get money back. Additional payment: consumption cost more.

advance.text: The monthly payment made in advance to the supplier. The annual bill compares the total with the actual costs.

workingPrice.text: The price per unit consumed — ct/kWh, for water ct/m³.

basePrice.text: A fixed amount per month, independent of consumption.

specialPayment.text: A refund, additional payment or extra advance outside the monthly advance. “With effect” also changes the future advance.

offer.text: A tariff you do not have — from a comparison site, for example. It only affects the tariff comparison, never balance, forecast or contract status. Technically it is a shadow contract.

switchDate.text: The first day a new tariff could supply — from contract end and notice period. The cancellation must reach the supplier by the notice deadline.

noticeDeadline.text: The last day the cancellation must reach the supplier. If missed, a contract that renews unless cancelled is extended.

breakEven.text: The annual volume above which an offer is cheaper than your contract. If it is far from your consumption, the decision holds even with an imprecise forecast. A dash means there is no crossing point: the offer is cheaper or dearer at any volume.

baseline.text: A date from which your home changed — insulation or a new heating system, for example. Evaluations start at the baseline date so old values do not distort the picture.

calorificValue.text: The energy content of one cubic metre of gas in kWh, as the supplier states it per period on the bill.

zNumber.text: Converts the measured gas volume to standard conditions (pressure, temperature). kWh = m³ × correction factor × calorific value.

cutoffDate.text: The day from which a new value applies — a new price or calorific value, for example. Up to the day before, the old one applies.

efficiency.text: Heating energy per m² and year (kWh/m²·yr). The home figure refers to the living area; the certificate-style figure calculates like a consumption-based energy certificate (weather-adjusted, usable area; until 2026 on net, from 2027 on gross calorific value). Not an official certificate.

feedIn.text: Solar power you deliver to the grid. The remuneration is revenue — more is better here.

selfConsumption.text: Solar power you use yourself: generation minus feed-in. It replaces grid power — the saving is calculated with your unit price.

autarky.text: The share of your electricity consumption covered by your own system.

selfConsumptionRate.text: The share of the solar energy generated that you use yourself.

estimated.text: A reading that was estimated rather than read — often by the supplier. It counts but stays marked.

tankBook.text: For heating oil and pellets, consumption follows from initial stock, deliveries and known stock levels (delivery “to full”, tank reading). Between two known levels it is calculated, afterwards estimated.

subMeter.text: A sub-meter measures part of another meter and is subtracted from it so that nothing counts twice. A group only combines meters for the overview.

co2Avoided.text: Solar power replaces grid power. The calculation uses the CO₂ factor of grid electricity (Settings → Utilities & billing) — this much CO₂ would otherwise have been emitted. Simplified: manufacturing the system is not included.

periodCapture.text: A way of recording besides meter readings: each period holds the consumption itself, for example from the monthly consumption information. The app spreads it over the months to the day; after that everything works as with meter readings.

uvi.text: Since 2022, tenants with remotely read meters in Germany must be told their heating and hot-water consumption every month, with the previous month, the same month last year and an average user (HeizkostenV § 6a). The values can be entered as consumption per period.

prepayment.text: What a tenant pays the landlord every month for heating and operating costs. The service charge statement compares it with the actual costs.

utilityStatement.text: The landlord’s annual statement. In Germany it must arrive within twelve months of the end of the billing period; objections are possible up to twelve months after receipt (BGB § 556). Both deadlines appear in the calendar.

dhw.text: The heat used by a hot-water meter, calculated under HeizkostenV § 9: 2.5 kWh per m³ and degree above 10 °C. 1 m³ at 60 °C is 125 kWh. A calculated value, not a measurement.

co2Price.text: Since 2021 suppliers of gas and heating oil in Germany pay a price for every tonne of CO₂ and pass it on in the unit price: 55 euros fixed in 2025; in 2026 auctioned within a corridor of 55 to 65 euros – bills and heating cost statements use 60 euros per tonne. The app shows it – it is not a surcharge. It is calculated with the standard BEHG factors; wood, pellets and electricity carry none.

co2Split.text: In German rented homes, tenant and landlord share the CO₂ costs in ten stages (CO2KostAufG): below 12 kg CO₂ per m² and year the tenant bears everything, from 52 kg the landlord 95%. The value is rounded to one decimal place.

dynamicTariff.text: An electricity tariff whose unit price follows the wholesale price (§ 41a EnWG). It is billed per quarter hour with a smart metering system. The app estimates it with the monthly wholesale average plus a mark-up — an approximation, not a substitute for the bill.

module14a.text: The grid operator may throttle heat pumps, wall boxes, air conditioners and storage above 4.2 kW that went into operation from 2024 during bottlenecks – never below 4.2 kW; in return the grid fee drops. Module 1: a fixed amount per year. Module 2: a separate meter with 40% of the grid unit price. Module 3: time-variable grid fees on top of module 1.

jaz.text: How much heat a heat pump makes from one kWh of electricity, measured over a year: heat ÷ electricity. Needs a heat meter on the heat pump. In a field test, air/water units reached about 3.4, brine/water 4.3.

profileFactor.text: Your wholesale price per kWh (weighted by consumption) divided by the market average. Below 1: you use more when electricity is cheap; above 1: more when it is expensive.

typicalDay.text: The energy flow of an average day in the month: for each quarter hour (local time), the average over all days of the month with readings. It shows the pattern — say, when the midday sun charges the battery — not a real day.

billingYear.text: The period of a supplier’s annual bill, for example September to August. The app takes it from the recorded bills, otherwise from the settlement date of the utility; a change of supplier ends it on the last day with the old supplier. You can switch to it on the utility page, the overview and the analysis.

scenario.text: A calculation with changed assumptions — colder winter, insulation, different tariff — against the baseline, the forecast from your data. A scenario is a model calculation, not a measurement: it shows in which direction and how strongly a change works.

runningYear.text: In the current year, the calendar year counts the standing charge and advance payment of the month of the last reading in full, the billing year only the days up to the reading — whole years are the same in both views.

support.title: Questions and bugs
support.text: Questions, requests and bug reports go to the GitHub project. A bug report is easier with the details from the diagnostics under Settings → System.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.text: Everything stays on your server: no accounts, no ads, no telemetry. The app only talks to Open-Meteo — for the daily weather sync (only the location rounded to about 1 km, can be switched off under Settings → Weather data) and for the place search when you use it — and, only if you enter them, to your own text recognition service and your evcc in your home network. When you tap “Load from SMARD”, the app fetches wholesale electricity prices from the Federal Network Agency; nothing of yours is sent.

heat.title: District heating or heat?
heat.text: You buy district heating yourself from the supplier – with your own contract, energy and standing charge and a bill; that is what the “District heating” type is for. Heat is measured heat without a supply contract of your own: in a rented flat it is paid through the service charge statement (with the monthly consumption information), in your own house it is the heat output of the heat pump – that is what “Heat” is for. The example households “Owner-occupied flat with district heating”, “I rent my home” and “Own house with heat pump and solar” show all three cases.

control.title: Control with evcc or Home Assistant
control.text: The Energietracker switches nothing. evcc or Home Assistant control the battery, wallbox and heat pump – with solar power, in cheap hours or at negative wholesale prices. The Energietracker checks the result: charging sessions from evcc with their solar share, meter readings via Home Assistant, the dynamic tariff check with wholesale prices and the charging record show what the control achieved.

levels.title: Simple first, everything later
levels.text: The level at the top next to day/night decides how much you see: beginners get three answers on the overview, the experienced level adds tariff switch, bill check and analyses, experts see everything. Everything is calculated at every level – you can switch at any time. To try it out, the setup assistant loads an example household that fits you.

sharedMeters.title: Shared flat with shared meters
sharedMeters.text: One shared main meter plus a meter of its own for a room or a device: create the second one as a sub-meter of the main meter. The app deducts it from the main meter – the total stays correct, and the share for splitting the costs appears as a figure of its own. The contract belongs to the main meter.

homeAssistant.title: Smart home with Home Assistant
homeAssistant.text: Home Assistant already reads your meters? Then it sends the readings to the Energietracker every evening: create an API token in the settings, give each meter an alias, paste the ready-made template into Home Assistant. A second value on the same day replaces the first instead of doubling it.

pvHeatPump.title: Solar household with a heat pump
pvHeatPump.text: Feed-in and generation as utilities of their own, the heat pump as a sub-meter of the grid connection: the app shows the electricity balance, self-sufficiency and self-consumption, plus the heat pump’s electricity without doubling the total. A heat meter adds the seasonal performance factor, charging and discharging meters add the battery.

landlord.title: Landlord with several units
landlord.text: A meter with its own contract for each flat and utility: the consumption view shows every meter with consumption, costs and balance, the overview the total per utility. Several meters of the same utility in one flat form a group, if you like with one contract for the whole group. The app does not prepare service charge statements for tenants.

wallbox.title: Wallbox and company car
wallbox.text: The wallbox as a sub-meter of the grid connection with the role “Wallbox (EV charger)”, read monthly – by hand, via Home Assistant or with the charging sessions from evcc. Its consumption view shows the charging record for the employer: contract price with a share of the standing charge or a flat rate, as CSV or PDF. The total stays correct.

flex.title: Valuing flexibility
flex.intro: When is it worth using power, and how much does shifting bring? The traffic light shows cheap and expensive hours, “Your lever” what it can bring in a year. The calculation uses consumption, generation and the wholesale price per quarter hour; control happens elsewhere (evcc, Home Assistant, the battery itself).

lever.title: Your lever
lever.lead: What shifting can bring in a year: consumption moves into the cheapest quarter hours of its day (the car: while it is plugged in), at most at the appliance’s highest measured power. Today’s pattern is one of the options, so no lever is negative.
lever.total: Together up to {eur} a year incl. VAT (biggest lever per appliance), of which {real} on your tariff.
lever.upper: Upper limit: the cheapest quarter hours are known the day before (day-ahead). Wholesale price with {vat} VAT, as a dynamic tariff bills it, without its mark-up, levies and grid fee; solar power at unit price minus feed-in tariff; module 3 with the amounts on the contract, net amounts plus VAT.

evSessions.other: Car: shifted only while it is plugged in — plug-in times from {count} charging sessions in evcc.

inboxDraft.title: Household from documents
inboxDraft.subtitle: One draft across all read documents: meters, contracts, readings, bills. You only check what is marked.

without.one: {count} document adds nothing to the draft
without.other: {count} documents add nothing to the draft

count.noQuestions: Nothing needs you: every value is quoted from the document.

inboxDraft.empty: No document read yet. File your supplier mail in the inbox and have it read – the draft starts with the first read document and grows with each one.
inboxDraft.entryHint: All documents at once: meters, contracts, readings and bills, only doubtful values to check.

queue.running: Still reading: {done} of {total}. The draft grows with it.

inboxDraft.choose: The documents disagree – which value is right?
inboxDraft.applyHint: The app makes a backup first. Everything goes through the same checks as manual entry; existing data is only overwritten where you confirm it.
inboxDraft.stale: The draft has changed in the meantime (for example because more documents were read). It has been reloaded – please look at it again.

partly.one: {count} part not taken over – see below
partly.other: {count} parts not taken over – see below

finding.gap: Gap between two contracts: {from} to {to} without a contract. The dates stay as the documents state them.
finding.overlap: Two contracts overlap from {from} to {to}. The later start applies; the dates stay as the documents state them.
finding.falling: The meter reading falls on {date} from {a} to {b} with no meter change in the documents – probably a new meter (suggestion below).
finding.chain_mismatch: The closing reading and the opening reading of the next bill do not match ({a} and {b} around {date}). Both readings need checking.
finding.duplicate: Probably a duplicate: {name} has the same content as {of} and counts once.
finding.no_meter: {name}: Without a meter or contract number the document fits several meters. Assign it in the document itself.
finding.same_supplier: {name} and {of}: treated as the same supplier – same meter, same time, a shared name.
finding.invoice_wp: {name}: energy price from {date} {invoice} instead of {chain} from the confirmation or price change. The chain is taken over; “Check a bill” shows the difference.
finding.invoice_bp: {name}: standing charge from {date} {invoice} instead of {chain} a month from the confirmation or price change. The chain is taken over; “Check a bill” shows the difference.
finding.start_from_invoice: Contract {provider}: start moved forward to {from} – the first bill of the same contract begins before the {to} in the confirmation.
finding.bill_corrected: Corrected bill: {name} replaces {of}. The corrected version is taken over, the earlier one stays as a receipt.
finding.start_near: {provider}: start {from} according to the document, {date} on record – the same contract (up to 7 days apart); the recorded start stays.

missing.old_final: {utility}: meter change on {date} without the closing reading of the old meter. Enter the meter swap with that reading by hand.
missing.working_price: {utility}: the energy price for {provider} is in no document.

missing.base_price_gap: {utility}: no document names a standing charge for {provider} from {from} to {to}.

missing.meter_choice: {utility}: which meter does {meter} belong to? Possible: {meters}. Assign a document to the right meter in the inbox and the draft takes it over – if it is a new meter, add it with this number.
